description: Research workspace for SchedulePoint application analysis: navigation structure, screen inventory, evidence collection, the Phase 12 edge-case/QA catalogue, and a final coverage-reconciliation audit. Broad research against ischedule.md is closed after Phase 12 and reconfirmed closed after the coverage audit.

structure.RESEARCH-RULES.md: Read-only navigation rules for Claude for Chrome: permitted controls, prohibited mutating actions, and the 'if uncertain, do not click' policy governing all ischedule.md exploration
structure.reports/: Written findings, indices, and tracking documents
structure.reports/inbox/: Unsorted/raw notes and evidence awaiting triage into the main reports
structure.screenshots/navigation/: Evidence of top-level nav, menus, and routing between major sections
structure.screenshots/schedule/: Evidence of scheduling/calendar screens and interactions
structure.screenshots/requests/: Evidence of request workflows (submission, approval, status)
structure.screenshots/picklist/: Evidence of picklist/shift-bid or selection-list screens
structure.screenshots/admin/: Evidence of admin-facing configuration and management screens
structure.screenshots/errors/: Evidence of error states, validation messages, and failure modes

namingConvention: Use generic, descriptive filenames only: <area>-<screen-or-state>-<sequence>.png (e.g. schedule-week-view-01.png, requests-submit-error-02.png). No personal names, phone numbers, patient identifiers, employee IDs, or other sensitive data in filenames or file contents.

phaseReports.title: Technical observations: frontend stack, routes, API resource catalogue (API-01..14), request/response patterns, auth/session, real-time (SignalR), caching/performance, client-vs-server responsibility matrix, SchedulePoint implications (T-01..T-10)
phaseReports.mergePolicy: 17-section structure per instructions; all identifiers sanitized (GROUP_ID/USER_ID/PICKLIST_ID/YYYY-MM-DD placeholders); no request replayed/modified/guessed, no cookie/token/storage values recorded (names only). Major findings: confirms a SignalR 'picklist' real-time hub exists (closes part of Phase 8's gap without triggering a live picklist); a concrete N+1-style duplicate-request defect (~25-40x identical calls from one click); a hashed-email leak to Gravatar on every page load; Zendesk support widget silently 503-broken on every page load.

phaseReports.title: Edge cases and QA catalogue: 175 prioritized SchedulePoint test cases across 13 categories, with evidence classification, contradictions register, and carried-forward gaps
phaseReports.status: complete; final broad research phase against ischedule.md
phaseReports.mergePolicy: Derived entirely from reports 01-10 with no new source-site navigation. Adds stable QA IDs (QA-TEN/AUTH/SCH/REQ/OPP/PICK/RPT/NOT/DATE/CON/SEC/PERF/A11Y-NNN) referencing existing screen, workflow, lifecycle, RA/F, API and T IDs rather than redescribing them. Every case carries one of five evidence classifications (OBSERVED, INFERRED, UNRESOLVED, SP-REQ, SP-IMP); inferences are never promoted to observations. Encodes six hard SchedulePoint requirements: SP-HR-1 no email-derived identifier to any third-party avatar provider; SP-HR-2 one user action must not generate duplicate equivalent requests; SP-HR-3 visible keyboard-focus indicator on every interactive element; SP-HR-4 accessible name on every icon-only control; SP-HR-5 every critical workflow keyboard-operable; SP-HR-6 errors/validation/status changes programmatically communicated. Records 7 unresolved contradictions (C-01..C-07) without silently resolving them, and carries 14 gaps forward as future SchedulePoint tests. 67 MVP blockers. No source-site data created, modified, submitted, downloaded, imported, exported, or invalidated; no safety incident.

phaseReports.title: Final coverage audit: navigation-to-report reconciliation across both group memberships, 7 newly discovered passively-observed surfaces, cross-group corroboration of one open contradiction, and one live-picklist state noted but deliberately not pursued
phaseReports.mergePolicy: Reconciles the full navigation surface (both groups, all 34 previously-documented screens) against reports 01-12 via passive href/hidden-DOM inspection only (no clicks on any Add/New/Create/Send/Save/Publish-type control). Adds 7 new stable IDs (CAL-01, SM-10..SM-14, NAV-03) for surfaces found via the same zero-click hidden-dialog-inspection technique Phase 10 used for the Print-menu discovery. Resolves or partially resolves unresolved-questions.md #39, #58, #60, #61, #62. Confirms full 22-route sidebar/admin parity across both groups (reconfirms GRP-01). Discovers incidentally that a live picklist is active in the account's other group membership; per this audit's explicit brief, deliberately does not pursue Dashboard/Picklist Manager/room-selection investigation of it — records only that the aggregate progress-bar state exists. No mutation, no safety incident. Does not begin Phase 13.

phaseReports.title: Product glossary: 75 normalized terms (TERM-001..075) reconciling iSchedule.MD vocabulary into a single SchedulePoint terminology, with split/merge/rename/avoid dispositions
phaseReports.mergePolicy: Derived entirely from reports 01-11 plus the final coverage audit; no source-site navigation. Introduces the TERM-### namespace (no collision with existing F-##, SM-##, RA-##, WF-##, LC-##, ADM-##, QA-* namespaces). Every term carries 10 required fields including preferred SchedulePoint term, source term(s), classification (OBS/INF/UNR/SP-REQ/SP-REC), confidence, ambiguities, and a retain/rename/split/merge/introduce/avoid disposition. Preserves rather than resolves contradictions C-01, C-02, C-03, C-05, C-06. Flags the three-way '...Group' naming collision (Staff Group / Shift Group / Valid Group), the four-way overload of 'Pick', the three-way overload of 'Shift', and the two unrelated uses of 'Publish' and 'Transfer'. Marks TERM-062 (instant-commit Add) and TERM-070 (clinical case detail) as explicit do-not-replicate/exclude items.

phaseReports.title: Feature inventory: 46 deduplicated capabilities (FEAT-001..054) with SchedulePoint dispositions, a Mermaid MVP dependency map, and four contradiction-blocked decisions
phaseReports.mergePolicy: Derived entirely from reports 01-11 plus the final coverage audit; no source-site navigation. Introduces the FEAT-### namespace. Merges by stable ID -- a capability documented across five source reports gets one entry. 46 distinct features carrying 52 disposition assignments (features may hold a dual disposition where capability and mechanism differ): 25 MVP, 10 POST-MVP, 6 REQUIRES DECISION, 6 SOURCE DEFECT -- DO NOT REPLICATE, 4 REPLACE WITH ORIGINAL SCHEDULEPOINT DESIGN, 1 EXCLUDED, 0 DEFERRED. Disposition table is generated programmatically from the feature blocks, not hand-tallied. Six source defects catalogued explicitly (FEAT-047 delete-by-default inspection click; FEAT-048 instant-commit Add; FEAT-049 request amplification; FEAT-052 third-party avatar identifier leak; FEAT-053 silently broken third-party widget; FEAT-054 accessibility baseline failures), mapping to hard requirements SP-HR-1..SP-HR-6. FEAT-051 (clinical case detail) EXCLUDED from MVP. Contradictions C-02, C-03, C-04, C-06 preserved as explicit blocking decisions with options, consequences, and a recommended direction marked pending product-owner approval.

phaseReports.title: Domain model: inferred source model plus a proposed clean-room SchedulePoint conceptual model of 44 entities (ENT-001..040), with ERD and five matrices
phaseReports.mergePolicy: Derived entirely from reports 01-11 plus the final coverage audit; no source-site navigation. Conceptual product model only -- explicitly not a database schema or technical architecture. Introduces the ENT-### namespace. 44 entities, each with purpose, fields, required/optional, relationships, ownership scope, lifecycle, audit requirement, retention, sensitivity classification, source evidence, confidence, related features, related QA cases, and unresolved decisions. Includes a Mermaid ERD, a tenant-ownership matrix (all 44 entities reconciled programmatically against the blocks), a sensitive-data matrix, an audit-requirement matrix, a source-to-SchedulePoint entity mapping, and 12 concepts intentionally redesigned rather than copied. Key structural decisions: role lives on Membership (ENT-006); ShiftType, Assignment and Credit are three separate entities; published schedules are immutable versions (ENT-016) because the source has no rollback control; Notification and NotificationAttempt are added because the source has no delivery record at all; AuditEvent generalises the source's per-cell log and makes it queryable. NO PATIENT-LEVEL ENTITY EXISTS IN THIS MODEL -- deliberate exclusion carried as an architectural requirement. Contradictions C-02 (permission model), C-03 (request entity), C-04 (real-time delivery) preserved as blocking open decisions D-02, D-03, D-07.

phaseReports.title: State machines: 21 conceptual lifecycles (STM-001..021) with 11 Mermaid diagrams, preserving C-02 and C-04 as explicit blocking unresolved decisions
phaseReports.mergePolicy: Derived entirely from reports 01-11 plus the final coverage audit; no source-site navigation. Conceptual lifecycles only -- no API, endpoint, storage mechanism, or framework specified. Introduces the STM-### namespace. All 21 required lifecycles covered: build, review, publication, revision, ON/OFF requests, time-off, vacation, opportunities, offers, swaps, transfer approval, picklist preparation, picklist execution, room selection, notification delivery/retry, escalation, user invitation, suspension/deactivation/archive, proxy authorization, document lifecycle, calendar-feed token. Each carries purpose, actors, states, initial/terminal, transitions with actor + precondition + server guard, side effects, audit, notifications, invalid transitions, cancellation, expiry, retry, recovery, concurrency, idempotency, evidence, confidence, unresolved decisions, and QA cases. Six universal rules applied throughout (server-enforced transitions, membership-scoped authorization, mandatory audit, idempotency, keyboard reachability, fail-closed). HONESTY RULE: no transition was invented to make a diagram look complete -- 11 of 21 machines carry Low confidence, reflecting how much source behaviour was unobservable without prohibited mutating actions. C-02 (picklist permission model) and C-04 (real-time vs polling) are preserved as explicit BLOCKING unresolved decisions on STM-012/013/014, each with options, consequences, and a recommended direction pending product-owner approval.

phaseReports.title: Research completion and handoff: 21-section summary for the product-definition and architecture stages
phaseReports.mergePolicy: Handoff summary, not a digest -- deliberately does not reproduce the other reports, but points to where detail lives. Covers scope, method and safety boundary (including the one Phase 8 safety incident and the deliberately-unopened live picklist), the coverage-audit conclusion, confirmed capabilities, roles, workflows, business rules, technical observations, six source defects, accessibility findings, privacy and security findings, the six SchedulePoint hard requirements plus carried architectural requirements, recommended MVP (25 features) and post-MVP (10) scope, exclusions, product-owner decisions required (C-02 and C-03 blocking), architecture decisions required (C-04 blocking, plus A-01..A-07), 14 remaining evidence gaps in priority order, 6 required future test environments (MULTI, CONC, LIVE-SIM, PERF, A11Y, DR), the recommended next phase, and a formal research-completion declaration. States explicitly that broad research against ischedule.md is complete, the coverage audit found no missing top-level module, seven subordinate surfaces were documented, an active picklist was observed but deliberately not opened, live picklist execution remains the largest observational gap, remaining gaps do not block consolidation, SchedulePoint must be clean-room, and the next phase is product reconciliation and product-owner decisions -- not application coding.

phaseReports.title: Public-source functionality-gap addendum: 70 public claims (PUB-001..070) reconciled against the consolidated research; 19 gaps; 5 new contradictions (C-08..C-12); 17 proposed Phase 13 amendments
phaseReports.mergePolicy: Targeted reconciliation performed after Phase 13 and before architecture. Public sources inspected 2026-07-30: the ischedule.md homepage (all 6 capability pillars, 7 long-form product sections, ALL 8 FAQ answers expanded, testimonials, footer), the public pricing PDF (full text extracted), and the application's own public /users/login and /users/forgotpassword pages. Authenticated corroboration was deliberately narrow -- five already-safe read-only screens revisited only to check whether a specific public claim has a visible corresponding feature. NO broad re-crawl. THE ACTIVE PRODUCTION PICKLIST WAS NEVER OPENED. No form submitted; no mutating action. Introduces the PUB-### namespace. Every claim carries source URL + section, one primary classification, and a mapping to existing TERM/FEAT/ENT/STM/QA IDs or a proposed amendment. Resolves unresolved questions #14, #29 and #76 from public/observed evidence. Records 19 gaps (GAP-01..19) including three newly-observed authenticated Group Settings fields (Pick List Access, Payment Due Date, Convert to lowercase when importing) that no prior phase documented. Adds contradictions C-08 (automated scheduling central vs under-weighted), C-09 (de-identification claim vs observed clinical detail), C-10 (push notifications claimed but absent), C-11 (group email address claimed but absent), C-12 (edition model absent). C-02 and C-04 remain explicitly unresolved and blocking. Automated scheduling is classified REQUIRED FOR PRODUCTION; manual scheduling is ADMINISTRATIVE FALLBACK OR OVERRIDE only. Reports 12-16 were NOT modified; 17 amendments (AMD-01..17) are recorded by stable ID for a later coherent pass.

phaseReports.title: Targeted sandbox test plan: 39 authorized tests (SBX-001..035 incl. variants) covering every behaviour that cannot be safely verified in production
phaseReports.mergePolicy: Companion to report 17. Introduces the SBX-### namespace. Defines seven environments (MULTI, CONC, LIVE-SIM, PERF, A11Y, DR, and a new INTEG integration sandbox), ten synthetic test accounts spanning all six roles plus a cross-tenant account and a per-membership role-divergence account, and four controlled notification endpoints. Each test specifies objective, roles, environment, synthetic data, setup, exact safe sequence, expected evidence, notification destination, success criteria, cleanup, related feature/QA IDs, and whether it gates architecture, beta, or production. Absolute constraint: NO test may run against the live production organization, and the active production picklist must never be opened. Includes a Mermaid execution-dependency graph, risk controls, cleanup and evidence-capture requirements, four gates (architecture, beta, production, connector-release), and a coverage table proving every unobservable lifecycle has a test or a documented justification.
